note: Carthage as a simulated city in the island scenario (Phase 2). Its bodies and men are history, carded in docs/research/island-405-395.md; Aristotle wrote about fifty years after this decade, so his picture may not fit 405 exactly. Every power, mood, store, threshold and action rule here is invention.

blocs.name: the Elders
blocs.detail: The council of the great merchant houses. They count silver and fear for trade.
blocs.wants: Rebuild while trade pays; war only if Carthage's anger is 8 or more, or a Punic town falls; peace once an army is lost or plague is in the city.

facts.text: The kings bring business to the people only if they and the Elders disagree.
facts.quote: The reference of some matters and not of others to the popular assembly rests with the kings in consultation with the Elders in case they agree unanimously, but failing that, these matters also lie with the people

facts.text: Members of the senate were sent with silver to hire mercenaries.
facts.quote: dispatched members of the senate with large sums of money to recruit mercenaries in Europe

blocs.basis: Invention from a later description: Aristotle, Politics 1273a, written about 340 to 330 BC, two generations after this decade. Diodorus names only a senate for 397 (14.47.2). Kept with its quotes, so the source is visible.

blocs.name: the Hundred
blocs.detail: The highest magistracy, chosen by the Boards of Five. In the game they guard Carthage's hold on Sicily and its tribute.
blocs.wants: Keep the tribute; war if Carthage's anger is 6 or more, or a tribute town or Punic town is lost; peace only after two armies are lost.

facts.text: The Boards of Five elect the Hundred.
facts.quote: the election by these boards of the supreme magistracy of the Hundred

blocs.basis: Invention from a later description: Aristotle, Politics 1273a, written about 340 to 330 BC, two generations after this decade. Diodorus names only a senate for 397 (14.47.2). Kept with its quotes, so the source is visible.

blocs.name: the people of Carthage
blocs.detail: The assembly. When the kings and the Elders disagree, the people decide, and anyone may speak against a proposal.
blocs.wants: Rebuild after the plague; war if Carthage's anger is 7 or more, or a Punic town falls, and stay at war once in it; peace when plague is in the city.

facts.text: In the assembly the people have the sovereign decision.
facts.quote: the people have the sovereign decision, and anybody who wishes may speak against the proposals introduced

blocs.basis: Invention from a later description: Aristotle, Politics 1273a, written about 340 to 330 BC, two generations after this decade. Diodorus names only a senate for 397 (14.47.2). Kept with its quotes, so the source is visible.

blocs.name: the Libyan subjects
blocs.detail: The farmers of Carthage's African land. They have no vote, but they fill the levies, and if they rise, Carthage must turn home.
blocs.wants: To be left alone. Every levy sours them; if they turn Rebellious, Carthage's goal becomes Quiet Libya.

facts.text: Plague struck Carthage's subjects in Libya before the war of 397.
facts.quote: the plague which had broken out among them and had destroyed the larger part of the inhabitants of Libya

facts.text: Carthage raised its army of 396 from all Libya and from hired men.
facts.quote: they gathered armaments from all Libya as well as from Iberia

facts.text: Given supreme command for the war of 396.
After the disaster at Syracuse he starved himself to death.
facts.quote: In the end he passed sentence of death upon himself and starved himself to death
no less than eighty thousand in number and under the command of Magon

people.name: Hanno the elder
people.role: Head of a great merchant house, for the Elders

people.name: Bomilcar
people.role: A man of the Hundred who wants a command

goals.name: Rebuild
goals.text: Carthage mends its losses and trades.

goals.name: Guard the tribute
goals.text: Carthage holds what the peace gave it.

goals.name: Peace at a price
goals.text: Carthage wants out of the war.

goals.name: Quiet Libya
goals.text: Carthage's own land is in revolt.

goals.name: Recover
goals.text: Carthage mends what it lost, courts the Sicilian towns, takes in the men you drove out, and makes ready to come back.
goals.note: Switch carthageReturns (thread 48 spec 1): Magon 'set about retrieving the Carthaginian cause after the disaster' (Diodorus 14.90.2-3); 'they constructed ships and made careful provision of supplies' (14.77.5). Numbers invention.

actions.name: Trade
actions.text: Carthage's ships trade along the coasts.

actions.name: Hire mercenaries
actions.text: Carthage sends men with silver to hire soldiers abroad.

actions.name: Raise a Libyan levy
actions.text: Carthage calls up its Libyan subjects.

actions.name: Build ships
actions.text: Carthage's yards build warships and transports.

actions.name: Garrison a town
actions.text: Carthage sends men to hold a town of its own in Sicily.

actions.name: Name a general
actions.text: The council gives one man the command.

actions.name: Send an army to Sicily
actions.text: Carthage ships an army to Sicily.

actions.name: Send more men
actions.text: Carthage ships more men to its army in Sicily.

actions.name: Send silver to the tyrant's enemies
actions.text: Carthaginian silver finds a man in Syracuse who hates you.

actions.name: Offer peace
actions.text: Carthage's envoys come to Syracuse with terms.

actions.name: Recall the army
actions.text: The council calls its army home.

actions.name: Propitiate the gods
actions.text: Carthage makes offerings to win back the gods.

actions.name: Quiet the Libyans
actions.text: Carthage remits a year's dues in Libya.

actions.name: Raid the coast
actions.text: Carthage's ships raid a Sicilian coast.
actions.note: Switch warFocus: in a lull of the war Carthage's fleet raids your coast, as Himilcon's squadron raided the harbour to draw off Dionysius' fleet (Diodorus 14.49.1-2). Numbers invention.

actions.name: Court a town
actions.text: Carthage's envoys court a Sicilian town.
actions.note: Switch warFocus: Magon 'showed kindness to the subject cities' (Diodorus 14.90.3). Numbers invention.

actions.name: Take in the exiles
actions.text: Carthage welcomes the men you drove out of Syracuse.
actions.note: Magon 'received the victims of Dionysius' wars' (Diodorus 14.90.3). Numbers invention.

notes_method: method: switch warFocus. Himilcon took Eryx by treachery (Diodorus 14.55.4); Magon 'showed kindness to the subject cities' (14.90.3). Hanno and Bomilcar are invented; their methods are invention.

returns.note: Switch carthageReturns (thread 48 spec 1, docs/council/2026-11-27-abroad.md). Every number is invention.
